answer: Each identity posts a 60-credit bond in the violet ledger and registers one endpoint in the atlas. Auditors send probes through the river of checks; an endpoint that signs each probe with its key keeps the bond, while a shared endpoint or duplicate signature slashes the bond and removes the identity. The k-th fake still needs an endpoint, server, and 60-credit bond, so 1,000 fakes lock 60,000 credits plus 1,000 servers, with no reuse. A rented-server farm fails because one key for two identities exposes both and both bonds are slashed. An honest agent posts one bond once.
